concept: A - Tosbi (two-faced turtle, 9 x MG90S, ESP32-S3 SuperMini, GC9A01)
method: Each product page was fetched with curl on 2026-10-24 and parsed from the shop's PRODUCT_DATA JSON (total_sale_price = KDV-included price; quantity = live stock). Robotistan, Direnc and Motorobit prices are USD-linked and move daily, by about +/-2%.

items.part: MG90S metal-gear micro servo, 180-degree (8 legs + 1 neck + 1 spare)
items.note: Concept price confirmed. The spare is dropped in the lean variant. Motorobit sells the same servo at 151.50. Lean variant buys 9 (no spare): -125.80.

items.part: ESP32-S3 SuperMini (Wi-Fi/BLE, 22.5 x 18 mm, RGB LED on GPIO48), in the head
items.note: Concept price confirmed. Direnc's SuperMini is cheaper at 342.89 but out of stock. The page lists only 11 free GPIO, so the display SPI, I2C, audio PWM, touch pads and battery ADC are a tight fit.

items.part: GC9A01 1.28in round IPS LCD, 240x240, SPI
items.note: Concept price confirmed; stock is low. Fallback: Motorobit round-PCB version at 545.40 (qty 112).

items.part: PCA9685 16-channel I2C PWM/servo driver (clone)
items.note: The concept's 'guide price' is now verified. The board has a single V+ terminal, so the two servo banks need their red leads rewired to the two MP1584 rails. Direnc's version is out of stock.

items.part: MPU6050 GY-521 6-axis IMU (flip and fall detection), replaces the concept's BMI160
items.note: The BMI160 is in stock at Direnc (127.86, qty 379, https://www.direnc.net/bmi160-gyro-sensor-modulu-6-dof-egim-ivmeolcer-jiroskop), but it would be the only item in a Direnc order and that parcel's shipping (~100-150) costs more than the 66 TL price difference. The GY-521 board is 21 x 16 mm, larger than the 11 x 12 mm space modelled for the BMI160, modelled at full size on the deck (fit checked, src/fit_report.json). To keep the BMI160, add Direnc shipping.

items.part: VL53L0X laser ToF module GY-53 (VL53L0X + STM32, 25 x 15.6 mm), cliff sensor: one per dome, looking forward-down out of a window under/over the neck stalk
items.note: Was 1 in the chin. The chin window pointed 35-55 deg ABOVE the horizon on face B, and the 25 x 15.6 board does not fit behind the chin (best of ~400 placements still cuts 58 mm3 into the head shell). Two modules now sit in the front of the domes (both domes stay one STL); the dome that is down does the edge sensing, so face A and face B are both covered (src/fit_check.py: no collision, no head occlusion over neck -40..+40). Stock 40, so 2 is fine. Optional (lean variant drops both). Both GY-53 answer at the same address in I2C mode; read one over its UART/PWM output or gate power per face. Cheaper Direnc CJMCU-530 / GY-VL53L0XV2 are out of stock; Direnc TOF050C (VL6180X) fit unchecked.

items.part: Orion 14500 3.7 V 900 mAh Li-ion cell (2S pack)
items.note: Cheaper than the guide's 105.48 (Direnc). It is a 3C cell (~2.7 A). No high-drain (>=4 A) 14500 was found in Turkish stock, so the concept's 4 A requirement is NOT met. Firmware must stage servo moves; expect sag during 4-leg push-ups.

items.part: 2S 5 A BMS Li-ion protection board
items.note: Concept price confirmed; 5 A rating per the title.

items.part: 2S 8.4 V USB-C charger board, 0.55 A charge current (39 x 18 x 6.3 mm)
items.note: Replaces the concept's Robolink 78 TL module. That module is in stock but its page states a 2 A charge current, about 2.2C for 900 mAh cells, which is too high. This board charges at 0.55 A (0.6C). Modelled at 39 x 18 x 6.3 on a printed upper deck over the PCA9685; fit checked (src/fit_report.json).

items.part: MP1584EN 3 A mini buck converter (2x servo bank at 5.5 V, 1x logic at 5.0 V)
items.note: Concept price confirmed. Set each output with a multimeter BEFORE connecting anything.

items.part: PAM8403 class-D amplifier with volume pot
items.note: The concept's 26.78 TL Robo90 board is in stock (qty 83), and Robolink has one at 22.50, but either would add a third parcel (~100+ shipping). This one rides in the Motorobit order. It is larger because of the pot; the pot can be desoldered. Modelled as a 24 x 21 board with an RV09-type pot (page gives no size), hung under the upper deck with the pot reaching down beside the PCA9685; fit checked.

materials: PLA mint (e.g. Elas/Porima 'Mint' or 'Su Yeşili'), about 100 g: 2 domes (same STL, printed twice dome-up at 0.12 mm), 4 hub eggs (split at the equator), 4 arms (top and bottom halves), 4 boots
PLA any colour, about 14 g: internal chassis, servo cradles, cell cradle
PLA cream/ivory, about 26 g: head front and back halves, stalk, tail
PLA coral, about 4 g: visor bezel and 2 hex 'pat me' plates. A pin-stripe in a 2nd colour needs a separate part or an AMS printer
PLA black, about 2 g: chin slot insert (now cosmetic), 2 ToF light tunnels in the domes, neck-slot liner, the band between the domes

PETG black, about 3.3 g: domed oval visor, printed dome-up. A curved top cannot be ironed, so it comes out semi-gloss with visible contour rings (as rendered). For a real gloss: wet-sand 400-2000 + clear coat (optional_visor_gloss, not in the totals).
TPU 95A, about 7 g: 4 toe capsules. Coral TPU is rarely stocked; studios usually have black, white or red
print.basis: Model mass from calc.py is 155 g of printed parts at the design wall thickness. A studio slicer adds supports, brims and purge, so about 180 g is billed. Typical Turkish studio rates in 2026: PLA 4-6 TL/g, PETG 6-8 TL/g, TPU 7-10 TL/g. One public tariff found lists PLA 5, PETG 6, TPU 7 TL/g and a 200 TL minimum (undated). pea3d.com 2026 gives 80-150 TL/h on professional machines plus material, and 20-40 TL/h on hobby printers. By gram: about 680-1020 TL PLA + about 30 PETG + about 70 TPU. Add a colour/material change surcharge of 6 jobs x 25-75 TL = 150-450 TL. Cross-check by hour: 18-26 h x 30-50 TL/h + about 200 TL filament = 740-1500 TL. No studio quote was obtained. The concept's 650-950 TL is too low for 6 materials and 0.12 mm domes. Shipping from the studio is counted under shipping_tl.

total_basis: Online-verified parts 4697.91 + local estimates 280-550 (pack welding 100-200, acrylic 80-150, glue/tape/marker 100-200) + print 900-1500 + shipping 170-300. Tools and the optional visor gloss excluded.

lean_variant.what: No cliff sensors at all (both GY-53, -846.70: NO desk-edge sensing on either face), no spare servo (-125.80), no separate USB-C breakout (put the charger's own port at the tail, -42.42), no acrylic window (the display glass shows through the visor opening, -100). Print in fewer colours: mint + cream PLA, black PETG visor, TPU toes, with the coral details printed in cream; this saves 1-2 colour jobs. Keeps the IMU, voice amp, touch and full self-righting.
lean_variant.total_basis: 3682.99 online parts + local 200-400 (pack welding 100-200 + glue/tape/marker 100-200, no acrylic) + print 800-1300 + shipping 170-300

changes_vs_concept: IMU: BMI160 (Direnc) became MPU6050 GY-521 (Robotistan, +65.67) to avoid a third parcel. The board is larger, so the deck slot must grow.
2S charger: Robolink 78 TL (2 A, too fast for 900 mAh) became Motorobit 2S 0.55 A USB-C at 181.80. It is 39 x 18 mm, larger than the 25 x 17 mm modelled.
PAM8403: Robo90 26.78 became the Motorobit pot version at 90.90 to ride in the same parcel.
14500 cells: 105.48 (guide) became Robotistan Orion at 94.95. They are 3C, NOT the >=4 A high-drain cells the concept asks for, and none were found in stock.

Added the forgotten items: power switch, perfboard, header, divider resistors, JST power leads, jumper ribbon, heat-shrink, solder, M2 nuts, USB data cable, spot-welded pack assembly, glue, tape and paint marker.
Print estimate raised from 650-950 to 900-1500 TL. Shipping raised from 150 to 170-300 TL, because the Motorobit parcel is under its 2,500 TL threshold and the studio parcel is extra.

Cliff sensing: the chin ToF looked 35-55 deg above the horizon on face B and its GY-53 board does not fit the chin. Two GY-53 (+423.35) now look out of the front of the domes; face A and face B both have edge sensing.
Fit: every BOM board is now modelled at its real size and checked with manifold3d booleans over all neck/hip/knee poses (src/fit_check.py, src/fit_report.json): 0 collisions.
